verses.zh: （安息日的诗歌。）称谢耶和华！歌颂你至高者的名！
verses.en: A psalm; a song for the Sabbath day.It is fitting[NOTE:1] to thank the Lord,and to sing praises to your name, O Most High.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 92. The psalmist praises God because he defeats the wicked and vindicates his loyal followers.
verses.commentary:
92:1-4 This strophe emphasizes praise. Notice the recurrent references to music. This would refer to
worship in the temple on a feast day.

- VERBS

- give thanks, Ps. 92:1 ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- sing praises, Ps. 92:1 ‒ BDB 274, KB 273, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- make glad, Ps. 92:4 ‒ BDB 970, KB 1333, Piel PERFECT

- sing for joy, Ps. 92:4 ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Piel IMPERFECT

- musical instruments (a. may define b. and, therefore, refer to only two instruments, cf. Ps. 33:2; 144:9)

- ten-stringed lute, Ps. 92:3 ‒ BDB 797

- harp, Ps. 92:3 ‒ BDB 614 II

- lyre, Ps. 92:3 ‒ BDB 490 (b. and c. are both mentioned in Ps. 57:8)

92:1 "to Your name" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "Most High" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B.

verses.zh: 用十弦的乐器和瑟，用琴弹幽雅的声音，早晨传扬你的慈爱；每夜传扬你的信实。这本为美事。
verses.en: It is fitting[NOTE:1] to proclaim your loyal love in the morningand your faithfulness during the night,
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.
verses.commentary:
92:2 This Psalm begins with three INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS.

- give thanks ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil

- sing praises ‒ BDB 274, KB 273, Piel

- declare ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil

Notice that number 3, "declare," also closes (inclusio) the Psalm at Ps. 92:15.
The declaration involves

- YHWH's lovingkindness, Ps. 92:2 (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed])

- YHWH's faithfulness, Ps. 92:2 (cf. Ps. 33:4; 143:1, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

- YHWH's uprightness, Ps. 92:15 (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS)

- YHWH's stability and strength (lit. "He is my rock"), Ps. 92:15

- YHWH's perfect character (lit. "there is no unrighteousness in Him," cf. Rom. 9:11; James 1:17),
Ps. 92:15

▣ "morning. . .night" These are parallel and are idiomatic for "always." The other option
is that they reflect the times of the daily sacrifice (i.e., 9 A.M., 3 P.M.
in the temple and, therefore, have a liturgical emphasis.

verses.en: to the accompaniment of a ten-stringed instrument and a lyre,to the accompaniment of the meditative tone of the harp.

verses.zh: 因你―耶和华藉着你的作为叫我高兴，我要因你手的工作欢呼。
verses.en: For you, O Lord, have made me happy by your work.I will sing for joy because of what you have done.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “it is fitting” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. Verses 1-3 are actually one long sentence in the Hebrew text, but this has been divided up into two shorter sentences in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style.
verses.commentary:
92:4 "what You have done" The two poetic lines of Ps. 92:4 repeat this thought
(i.e., Psalm 1, i.e., "The Two Ways," cf. Deut. 30:15,19). YHWH's work is

- the destruction of the wicked, Ps. 92:5-9 (esp. Ps. 92:7)

- the blessing of the righteous, Ps. 92:10-15

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的工作何其大！你的心思极其深！
verses.en: How great are your works, O Lord!Your plans are very intricate![NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
92:5-9 This strophe focuses on YHWH's activity toward

- a senseless man, Ps. 92:6a ‒ BDB 35 CONSTRUCT BDB 129

- a stupid man, Ps. 92:6b ‒ BDB 493, both #1 and #2 are used in Ps. 49:10; 94:8

- the wicked, Ps. 92:7a ‒ BDB 957

- he who does iniquity, Ps. 92:7b

- YHWH's enemies, Ps. 92:9 (twice) ‒ BDB 33, Qal PARTICIPLE

They are characterized as

- having no knowledge

- flourishing in this fallen world

- ultimately and permanently being destroyed (this is what the senseless and
stupid do not understand)

YHWH is characterized as

- having great works, cf. Ps. 40:5; 111:2

- deep thoughts (Qal PERFECT of BDB 770, KB 847 only here)

- on high forever (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ['olam])

- Ps. 92:15 is the praise due YHWH's faithful acts toward His faithful followers

verses.zh: 畜类人不晓得；愚顽人也不明白。
verses.en: The spiritually insensitive do not recognize this;the fool does not understand this.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “very deep [are] your thoughts.” God’s “thoughts” refer here to his moral design of the world, as outlined in vv. 6-15.

verses.zh: 恶人茂盛如草，一切作孽之人发旺的时候，正是他们要灭亡，直到永远。
verses.en: When the wicked sprout up like grass,and all the evildoers glisten,[NOTE:1] it is so that they may be annihilated.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand this.” The adjective בַּעַר (baʿar, “brutish”) refers to spiritual insensitivity, not mere lack of intelligence or reasoning ability (see Pss 49:10; 73:22; Prov 12:1; 30:2, as well as the use of the related verb in Ps 94:8).

verses.zh: 惟你―耶和华是至高，直到永远。
verses.en: But you, O Lord, reign[NOTE:1] forever.
notes: Heb “in order that they might be destroyed permanently.”sn God allows the wicked to prosper temporarily so that he might reveal his justice. When the wicked are annihilated, God demonstrates that wickedness does not pay off.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的仇敌都要灭亡；一切作孽的也要离散。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] look at your enemies, O Lord.Indeed,[NOTE:2] look at how your enemies perish.All the evildoers are scattered.

verses.zh: 你却高举了我的角，如野牛的角；我是被新油膏了的。
verses.en: You exalt my horn like that of a wild ox.[NOTE:1] I am covered[NOTE:2] with fresh oil.
notes: The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “to exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 75:10; 89:24; Lam 2:17).
verses.commentary:
92:10-15 This strophe focuses on YHWH's activities toward the righteous man (Ps. 92:12). Note
His activities on their behalf.

- exalted his horn (cf. Ps. 75:10; 112:9)

- anointed with fresh oil (cf. Ps. 23:5; 45:7; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE)

- would flourish like the palm (cf. Ps. 1:3; Jer. 17:8)

- would grow like the cedar (cf. Hosea 14:5-6)

- planted in YHWH's temple (cf. Ps. 52:8)

- would flourish in YHWH's courts (cf. Ps. 65:4; 84:10; 135:2)

- would yield fruit in old age

- full of sap and very green

- know YHWH is his rock and He is perfectly just (cf. Ps. 18:2; 94:22)

The rabbis interpreted this strophe as referring to an eschatological setting (cf. b. Rosh Hash. 31a; Rashi).
This may be right (cf. Ps. 92:7c).

92:10 "the wild ox" The LXX translated the Hebrew term BDB 910, ראם, as
"unicorn," which was followed by the King James Version. NKJV changes it to "wild ox."

This word is uncertain (KB 1163).

- wild bull (Akkadian root)

- wild buffalo

- white antelope (Arabic root)

- oryx (Targums)

- rhinoceros (Vulgate)

▣

NASB, NKJV
"I have been anointed"

NRSV
"you have poured over me"

TEV
"you have blessed me"

NJB
"you anoint me"

JPSOA
"I am soaked"

LXX
"my old age with thick oil"

Peshitta
"I will be anointed"

The VERB (BDB 117, KB 134, Qal PERFECT) usually
means "to mix" or "to confuse"; only here does it denote an anointing. This meaning possibly comes
from an Arabic root, "to moisten." The UBS Text Project (p. 363) gives "I am moistened" a "B" (some doubt)
rating.

verses.zh: 我眼睛看见仇敌遭报；我耳朵听见那些起来攻击我的恶人受罚。
verses.en: I gloat in triumph over those who tried to ambush me;[NOTE:1] I hear the defeated cries of the evil foes who attacked me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew verb בָּלַל (balal) usually has the nuance “to mix.” Here it seems to mean “to smear” or “to anoint.” Some emend the form to בַּלֹּתַנִי (ballotani; a second person form of the verb with a first person suffix) and read, “you anoint me.”

Heb “my eye gazes upon my walls.” See also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 56:2. The form שׁוּרָי shuray, “my walls”) should be emended to שׁוֹרְרָי (shoreray, “my foes” or perhaps “those who rebel against me” or “those who malign me”). See HALOT 1454 s.v. שׁוֹרֵר and also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 56:2.
verses.commentary:
92:11 If this Psalm reflects the praise of a King of Israel (LXX says David and "anointed,"
cf. Ps. 91:10b), then this verse may refer to a plot to overthrow the monarchy, which was discovered.

verses.zh: 义人要发旺如棕树，生长如黎巴嫩的香柏树。
verses.en: The godly[NOTE:1] grow like a palm tree;they grow high like a cedar in Lebanon.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “those who rise up against me, evil [foes], my ears hear.”
The singular is used in a representative sense, with the typical godly person being in view.

verses.zh: 他们栽于耶和华的殿中，发旺在我们　神的院里。
verses.en: Planted in the Lord’s house,they grow in the courts of our God.
verses.commentary:
92:13 "planted" This VERB (BDB 1060, KB 1570, Qal PASSIVE
PARTICIPLE) means "transplanted" and the PASSIVE implies, by God
(cf. Ps. 1:3; Jer. 17:8; Ezek. 17:10,22; 19:10,13; Hosea 9:13). Faithful followers start out as
unfaithful but the gracious God has an effect on them!

▣ "in the house of the Lord. . .in the courts of our God"
Notice the parallelism between YHWH and Elohim (cf. Gen. 2:4).

This imagery is referring to regular worship in the temple (cf. Ps. 23:6; 27:5), whether this is

- daily

- weekly

- feast days

is uncertain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

verses.zh: 他们年老的时候仍要结果子，要满了汁浆而常发青，
verses.en: They bear fruit even when they are old;they are filled with vitality and have many leaves.[NOTE:1]
notes: The cedars of the Lebanon forest were well-known in ancient Israel for their immense size.
verses.commentary:
92:14 This may be an allusion to Moses' 120 years of active service.

▣ "no unrighteousness in Him" YHWH is holy, no sin, no partiality, no changing
(cf. 2 Chr. 19:7; Deut. 32:4; Mal. 3:6; Rom. 9:14; Heb. 13:8; James 1:17).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Define the major theological theme describing YHWH's character in Ps. 92:2.

- lovingkindness

- faithfulness

- Are there two or three musical instruments listed in Ps. 92:3?

- What are the "work(s)" of YHWH's hands mentioned in Ps. 92:4b and 5a?

- How do Ps. 92:7 and 8 relate theologically?

- What does Ps. 92:11 relate to?

- How does Ps. 92: 12-14 relate to Psalm 1?

verses.zh: 好显明耶和华是正直的。他是我的磐石，在他毫无不义。
verses.en: So they proclaim that the Lord, my Protector,is just and never unfair.[NOTE:1]

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm uses agricultural growth imagery, as in Ps. 1:3, to describe one's spiritual life.

- negatively

- the wicked sprout up like grass, Ps. 92:7

- all who did iniquity flourished, Ps. 92:7

- positively

- the righteous man will flourish, Ps. 92:12

- he will grow, Ps. 92:12

- planted in the house of the Lord, Ps. 92:13

- they will flourish in the courts of our God, Ps. 92:13

- they will still yield fruit in old age, Ps. 92:14

- they will be full of sap and very green, Ps. 92:14

- There is a recurrent use of words beginning with פ (sound plays).

- sprouted (lit. "bud"), Ps. 92:7 ‒ BDB 827, KB 965

- did flourish, Ps. 92:7 ‒ BDB 821, KB 950

- scattered (lit. "be divided"), Ps. 92:9 ‒ BDB 825, KB 962

- all who do iniquity, Ps. 92:9 ‒ BDB 821, KB 950

- flourish (lit. "bud"), Ps. 92:12 ‒ BDB same as #1

- flourish (lit. "bud"), Ps. 92:13 ‒ same as #1

- There are no prayer requests (i.e., IMPERATIVES, JUSSIVES, COHORTATIVES), just
statements to the works of God.

- His character, Ps. 92:2,15

- His works

- creation, Ps. 92:5

- justice, Ps. 92:6-9

- blessings, Ps. 92:10-14
